     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DegreeZero
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)
    11	
    12	For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
    13	arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
    14	of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
    15	comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
    16	`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.
    17	
    18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
    19	  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
    21	  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
    22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
    23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
    25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
    27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
    28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
    29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
    30	  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
    31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
    32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
    33	-/
    34	
    35	set_option autoImplicit false
    36	
    37	universe u
    38	
    39	open CategoryTheory
    40	
    41	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    42	
    43	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    44	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    45	
    46	noncomputable section
    47	
    48	/-! ## The degree at a field point -/
    49	
    50	/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
    51	`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
    52	algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
    53	restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
    54	def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
    55	    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
    56	  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
    57	
    58	section DegAt
    59	
    60	variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    61	
    62	/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
    63	@[simp]
    64	theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
    65	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
    66	  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
    67	
    68	/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
    69	theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    70	    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
    71	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
    72	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
    73	        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
    74	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]
    75	
    76	/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
    77	theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    78	    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
    79	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
    80	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
    81	  rfl
    82	
    83	/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
    84	restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
    85	field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
    86	degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
    87	theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    88	    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
    89	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
    90	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
    91	  rw [← picEtMap_comp]
    92	
    93	/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
    94	theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
    95	    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    96	    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
    97	  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'
    98	
    99	end DegAt
   100	
   101	/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/
   102	
   103	variable (C) in
   104	/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
   105	classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
   106	degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
   107	def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
   108	  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
   109	    degAt lam t = 0}
   110	  one_mem' := by
   111	    intro K _ _ t
   112	    exact degAt_one t
   113	  mul_mem' := by
   114	    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
   115	    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
   116	  inv_mem' := by
   117	    intro a ha K _ _ t
   118	    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]
   119	
   120	/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
   121	theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
   122	    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
   123	      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
   124	          degAt lam t = 0 :=
   125	  Iff.rfl
   126	
   127	variable (C) in
   128	/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
   129	of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
   130	definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
   131	points. -/
   132	def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
   133	    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
   134	  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')
   135	    fun lam K _ _ t' => (degAt_picEtMap f (lam : picEt C T) t').trans (lam.2 K (t' ≫ f))
   136	
   137	/-- The underlying étale Picard class of a restricted degree-zero class — the
   138	naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/
   139	@[simp]
   140	theorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
   141	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
   142	    (pic0Map C f lam : picEt C T') = picEtMap C f (lam : picEt C T) :=
   143	  rfl
   144	
   145	variable (C) in
   146	/-- **The degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
   147	subfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes
   148	of degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of
   149	the Wave-4 representability statement (design §2.7): the Jacobian represents *this*
   150	functor. -/
   151	def pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
   152	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop)
   153	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Map C g.unop)
   154	  map_id T := by
   155	    ext lam U
   156	    exact congrArg (fun z : picEt C T.unop => z.1 U) (picEtMap_id C (lam : picEt C T.unop))
   157	  map_comp g h := by
   158	    ext lam U
   159	    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))
   160	
   161	@[simp]
   162	theorem pic0Functor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
   163	    (pic0Functor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :=
   164	  rfl
   165	
   166	@[simp]
   167	theorem pic0Functor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
   168	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
   169	    (pic0Functor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
   170	  rfl
   171	
   172	variable (C) in
   173	/-- The inclusion of the degree-zero subfunctor into the étale-sheafified relative
   174	Picard functor, as a natural transformation — the naturality square consumers cite
   175	(bundled form of `pic0Map_coe`). -/

1	/-
     2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
     5	-/
     6	import Mathlib
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RelPicFunctor
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor
    11	
    12	This file constructs the **étale-sheafified relative Picard functor**
    13	`Pic_{(C/k)ét}` of a smooth proper curve `C/k` and proves that it *is* a sheaf
    14	for the étale topology — the object whose representability is the project's
    15	central open obligation (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).
    16	
    17	## Why the sheafification is the right object
    18	
    19	The relative Picard presheaf `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
    20	(`Scheme.PicSharp.relPresheaf`, Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`) is in general **not
    21	a sheaf**, not even for the Zariski topology (Kleiman §2, L1292–L1302): a line
    22	bundle on `C ×_k T` can be trivial on each member of a cover of `T` without
    23	being trivial modulo `π_T^* Pic(T)`, because the gluing data is a `Pic`-class
    24	of the overlaps. Kleiman's representability theorem (§4 Thm. `th:main`) is
    25	therefore a statement about the associated **étale** sheaf, and it is that
    26	statement which is true over an arbitrary base field with no rational-point
    27	hypothesis.
    28	
    29	There are two ways to reach a sheaf, and they differ in what has to be
    30	supplied:
    31	
    32	1. assume `C` has a `k`-rational point. Then Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 says the
    33	   comparison `Pic_{C/k} → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is already bijective, so the plain
    34	   presheaf is the sheaf. This is *strictly weaker* than the challenge, whose
    35	   curve need not have a rational point, and it is the route the conditional
    36	   `Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` records;
    37	2. sheafify. Nothing is assumed about `C(k)`, and the sheaf axiom holds by
    38	   construction. This is the route realised here and the one the project
    39	   claims (owner decision of 2026-07-28).
    40	
    41	## The site
    42	
    43	Mathlib `v4.31` carries the big étale site on schemes,
    44	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleTopology = grothendieckTopology @Etale`
    45	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`). The relative Picard presheaf
    46	lives on the slice `Over (Spec k)` rather than on `Scheme`, so the topology is
    47	transported along the localisation of SGA 4 III 5.2.1, available in Mathlib as
    48	`GrothendieckTopology.over`: a sieve of `T : Over (Spec k)` covers iff the
    49	corresponding sieve of `T.left` covers étale-locally. That transport is where
    50	"the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`" becomes a definition rather than a parameter,
    51	and it is what lets the sheaf property below be a *theorem* rather than a
    52	hypothesis.
    53	
    54	## Main definitions
    55	
    56	* `Scheme.etaleTopologyOver k` — the étale topology on `(Sch/k) = Over (Spec k)`.
    57	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` — `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, a bundled
    58	  `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`, obtained by sheafifying the
    59	  relative Picard presheaf.
    60	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf_isSheaf` — the sheaf property, extracted as a
    61	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    62	    Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
    63	  (CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}).obj
    64	    (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
    65	
    66	/-- **The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, as a standalone statement.**
    67	
    68	The underlying presheaf of `PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` satisfies the sheaf axiom
    69	for the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`. This is `Sheaf.cond` of the bundled
    70	object, stated separately because it is the property consumers cite: a
    71	representing scheme for `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` exists only because the functor being
    72	represented is an étale sheaf (a representable functor is a sheaf for any
    73	subcanonical topology, so a non-sheaf can never be representable — which is
    74	exactly why the unsheafified `relPresheaf` needs a rational point).
    75	
    76	Proved, not assumed: sheafification produces a sheaf. -/
    77	theorem etaleSheaf_isSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    78	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    79	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
    80	  (etaleSheaf C).property
    81	
    82	/-- **The comparison map** `Pic_{C/k} ⟶ Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, i.e. the unit of the
    83	sheafification adjunction at the relative Picard presheaf.
    84	
    85	Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`) says this map is an isomorphism when `C` has a
    86	`k`-rational point (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic here). Over an
    87	arbitrary base field it is only a comparison: the honest object is the target,
    88	which is why the representability obligation is stated there. -/
    89	noncomputable def toEtaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    90	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    91	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
    92	  CategoryTheory.toSheafify (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
    93	
    94	/-- The universal property of the sheafification, in the form consumers use:
    95	every morphism from the relative Picard presheaf to (the underlying presheaf
    96	of) an étale sheaf factors uniquely through `toEtaleSheaf`.
    97	
    98	This is what makes `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` the *canonical* choice rather than one
    99	sheaf among many, and it is the step that turns a representing scheme for the
   100	sheaf into a universal receiver of relative Picard classes. -/
   101	noncomputable def etaleSheafHomEquiv {k : Type u} [Field k]
   102	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   103	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   104	    (G : Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
   105	    (etaleSheaf C ⟶ G) ≃ (PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ G.obj) :=
   106	  ((CategoryTheory.sheafificationAdjunction (etaleTopologyOver k)
   107	    AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).homEquiv (PicSharp.relPresheaf C) G)
   108	
   109	end PicSharp
   110	
   111	namespace PicScheme
   112	
   113	/-! ## §3. The set-valued functor that gets represented -/
   114	
   115	/-- **The functor whose representability is the project's central obligation**:
   116	the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor with its group structure
   117	forgotten,
   118	
   119	```
   120	picEt C : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1),   T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T).
   121	```
   122	
   123	Representability is a statement about the underlying set-valued functor; the
   124	group structure is transported back onto the representing scheme by Yoneda
   125	(`PicScheme.groupSchemeStructure`), exactly as for the unsheafified
   126	`picSharp`.
   127	
   128	Contrast with `picSharp C = relPresheaf C ⋙ forget`: that functor is
   129	representable only under a rational-point hypothesis (it is not even a
   130	Zariski sheaf otherwise), whereas *this* one is the object of Kleiman §4
   131	Thm. `th:main` and its representability needs no hypothesis on `C(k)`. -/
   132	noncomputable def picEt {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   133	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
   134	    (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1) :=
   135	  (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}
   136	
   137	/-- The comparison `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` of set-valued functors, the
   138	set-level shadow of `PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf`. An isomorphism under a
   139	`k`-rational point (Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5), a comparison in general.
   140	
   141	The source is written out as `PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget _` rather than as
   142	`picSharp C`, which is the *same functor by definition* but is declared in the
   143	downstream `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` (that file imports this one, so
   144	the name is not available here). -/
   145	noncomputable def picEtComparison {k : Type u} [Field k]
   146	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   147	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
   148	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} ⟶ picEt C :=
   149	  CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskerRight (PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf C)
   150	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})
   151	
   152	/-- **`picEt` is an étale sheaf of sets.**
   153	
   154	The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` survives forgetting the group structure,
   155	because the forgetful functor `AddCommGrpCat ⥤ Type` preserves the limits the
   156	sheaf condition is stated by. Together with the fact that a representable
   157	functor is a sheaf for a subcanonical topology, this is the structural reason
   158	the representability obligation is *consistent* as stated — which the
   159	unsheafified `picSharp` version was not, absent a rational point. -/
   160	theorem picEt_isSheaf_forget {k : Type u} [Field k]
   161	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   162	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
   163	    Presieve.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (picEt C) := by
   164	  have h := ((CategoryTheory.sheafCompose (etaleTopologyOver k)
   165	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})).obj (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C)).property
   166	  rw [CategoryTheory.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type] at h
   167	  exact h
   168	
   169	end PicScheme
   170	
   171	end Scheme

1	# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor on all test objects: the object level
     2	
     3	For a curve `C` over `k`, the étale-sheafified relative Picard group of an **affine**
     4	test is the one-step plus construction `PicEtAff C A` (étale-separatedness of the
     5	relative Picard presheaf makes one plus suffice — axiom (C1),
     6	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.CechKernelLemma`).  The frozen group-object interface forces
     7	the functor to exist on **all** of `Over (Spec k)`; following the resolution of the
     8	Layer-2 vehicle question (inbox I-0140), the extension is the *bespoke affine-opens
     9	limit*: a section over a test object `T` is a compatible family of plus classes over the
    10	affine opens of `T.left`, valued in `PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U)` via the section-ring
    11	algebras of `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtSections`.  The index poset is `Type u`-small,
    12	which is the point of the vehicle.
    13	
    14	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEt C T`: the limit, as the subgroup of the product over
    15	  `T.left.affineOpens` cut out by compatibility under restriction, with its `CommGroup`
    16	  structure; `picEt.eval` is evaluation at an affine open.
    17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.congr C e`: transport of plus classes along an isomorphism
    18	  of test algebras.
    19	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEtAffineEquiv C A`: **the affine comparison** — on an affine
    20	  test `overSpec k A`, evaluation at the top affine open is a group isomorphism
    21	  `picEt C (overSpec k A) ≃* PicEtAff C A` (the affine-opens poset of an affine test has
    22	  a terminal element, so the limit collapses).
    23	
    24	Functoriality in `T` — restriction along an arbitrary morphism of test objects, by
    25	gluing over basic-open refinements, licensed by (C1)-separatedness — is built on top of
    26	the Zariski sheaf property of `PicEtAff` in `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap`.
    27	-/
    28	
    29	set_option autoImplicit false
    30	
    31	universe u
    32	
    33	open CategoryTheory
    34	
    35	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    36	
    37	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    38	
    39	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra
    40	
    41	noncomputable section
    42	  rfl
    43	
    44	end PicEtAff
    45	
    46	/-! ## The affine-opens limit -/
    47	
    48	variable (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    49	
    50	/-- The compatible families over the affine opens of the test object, as a subgroup of
    51	the product of the affine-level plus groups: the value at a smaller affine open is the
    52	restriction of the value at a larger one. -/
    53	def picEtSubgroup :
    54	    Subgroup (Π U : T.left.affineOpens, PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U.1)) where
    55	  carrier := {s | ∀ (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1),
    56	    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s V) = s U}
    57	  one_mem' := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, map_one]
    58	  mul_mem' {a b} ha hb := fun U V h => by
    59	    rw [Pi.mul_apply, Pi.mul_apply, map_mul, ha U V h, hb U V h]
    60	  inv_mem' {a} ha := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.inv_apply, Pi.inv_apply, map_inv, ha U V h]
    61	
    62	/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor at an arbitrary test object**, object
    63	level: compatible families of affine-level plus classes over the affine opens of
    64	`T.left` — the bespoke affine-opens limit of `PicEtAff C ∘ Γ(T.left, ·)`.  On affine
    65	tests this is `PicEtAff` itself (`picEtAffineEquiv`); on general tests it is its
    66	canonical Zariski-continuous extension. -/
    67	def picEt : Type u :=
    68	  picEtSubgroup C T
    69	
    70	noncomputable instance : CommGroup (picEt C T) :=
    71	  inferInstanceAs (CommGroup (picEtSubgroup C T))
    72	
    73	namespace picEt
    74	
    75	variable {C T}
    76	
    77	/-- The compatibility of a section of `picEt` along an inclusion of affine opens. -/
    78	lemma compat (s : picEt C T) (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1) :
    79	    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s.1 V) = s.1 U :=
    80	  s.2 U V h
    81	
    82	@[ext]
    83	lemma ext {s t : picEt C T} (h : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens, s.1 U = t.1 U) : s = t :=
    84	  Subtype.ext (funext h)
    85	
    86	variable (C T) in
    87	/-- Evaluation of a section of `picEt` at an affine open, as a group homomorphism. -/
    88	def eval (U : T.left.affineOpens) : picEt C T →* PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U.1) :=
    89	  (Pi.evalMonoidHom (fun V : T.left.affineOpens => PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, V.1)) U).comp
    90	    (picEtSubgroup C T).subtype
    91	
    92	@[simp]

     8	/-!
     9	# THE ATLAS IS CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEOUS — each chart may carry its own `n`
    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` establishes that at a chart index legal at parameter
    12	`n` the coverage theorem's threshold is forced to equal `n`, and that at `n = g` the resulting
    13	hypothesis is false.  Both that file and the review it adjudicates (I-0660) then reason about
    14	"the" chart parameter, as though the atlas had one.
    15	
    16	**It does not, and this file proves it.**  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
    17	(`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) takes a family `f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf`
    18	indexed by an arbitrary `ι`, with `X : ι → Scheme` and a *per-index* certificate
    19	`hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`.  Nothing ties the `X i` together, so nothing ties
    20	their chart parameters together either: `mixedParamChart` below builds such a family from a
    21	per-index parameter `nn : ι → ℕ`, a per-index representation of `divFunctor C π (nn i)`, and a
    22	per-index chart index legal *at that index's own parameter*.
    23	
    24	## Why this matters, and it changes the shape of the residue
    25	
    26	The `b = n` calibration is per-chart.  So the question "can coverage use DAT-0a's threshold?"
    27	does not have to be answered uniformly: a point whose splitting field has threshold `b_L` can be
    28	covered by *the chart whose parameter is `b_L.toNat`*, and a different point by a different
    29	chart.  The I-0204 non-uniformity of `m` — no single exponent works for every fibre — is
    30	therefore **not** an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument for an atlas indexed by the
    31	threshold, which is what a heterogeneous family is.
    32	
    33	What this does **not** do, and the honest limit of the observation:
    34	
    35	* it does not produce the representations.  `mixedParamChart` takes `rep i` as a hypothesis, one
    36	  per parameter, and the divisor-representability lane supplies `divFunctor C π g` — a single
    37	  parameter.  So the heterogeneous atlas is *admissible* but not yet *inhabited* beyond `n = g`;
    38	* it does not discharge `IsChartUniv` at any index (still CERT-Σ-gated, `Pic0ChartPair.lean`);
    39	* it says nothing about local surjectivity, which is DAT-B B-6 and is what would actually consume
    40	  the freedom.
    41	
    42	So the correct statement of the residue, refining `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s: **B-5's step 3
    43	is a question about which parameters `divFunctor C π n` is representable at, not about
    44	reconciling one parameter with one threshold.**  If representability is available only at `n = g`
    45	then the slack must go into `Z` (and its legality is open, as recorded there); if it is available
    46	at every `n`, coverage can be assembled chart-by-chart against each fibre's own threshold and the
    47	`b = n` forcing is harmless.  That is a sharper question than either prior reading, and it is
    48	addressed to the divRep lane rather than to this one.
    49	
    50	## Main declarations
    51	
    52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamChart` — a chart family with a per-index chart parameter.
    53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart` — its `hf` clause is exactly a
    54	  per-index `IsChartUniv`, so heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate.
    55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamRepresentableBy` — such a family is admissible input to
    56	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  **This is the whole point**: the DAT-glue seam never sees a
    57	  chart parameter.
    58	-/
    59	
    60	set_option autoImplicit false
    61	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    62	
    63	universe u
    64	
    65	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    66	
    67	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    68	
    69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    70	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
    71	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    72	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    73	
    74	noncomputable section
    75	
    76	variable (C π) in
    77	/-- **A chart family whose chart parameter varies with the index.**
    78	
    79	Each index `i` carries its own degree parameter `nn i`, its own representing object `D i` of
    80	`divFunctor C π (nn i)`, its own twist exponent `m i` and chart index `Z i` — the latter legal
    81	*at `nn i`*, i.e. `deg_k (Z i) = (m i)·d₁ − nn i`, which is what `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`
    82	requires for that index's chart value to land in `pic⁰`.
    83	
    84	The construction is just `restrictChart` of `abelSigmaChart` applied pointwise; the content is
    85	that it *typechecks*, i.e. that the target `pic0SigmaSheaf C` is parameter-free. -/
    86	def mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
    87	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
    88	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
    89	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    90	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
    91	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
    92	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
    93	    yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme.{u})) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
    94	  restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)
    95	
    96	variable (C π) in
    97	/-- **Heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate**: the `hf` clause of a mixed-parameter
    98	family is exactly a per-index `IsChartUniv`, by definition of both.
    99	
   100	So a lane that can discharge CHART-U(c) *at one parameter* can discharge it index-by-index at
   101	different parameters, with no additional compatibility between them — there is no coherence
   102	condition across indices, because `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` imposes none. -/
   103	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
   104	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
   105	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
   106	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   107	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
   108	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
   109	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
   110	    (huniv : ∀ i, IsChartUniv C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i)) (i : ι) :
   111	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i) :=
   112	  huniv i
   113	
   114	variable (C π) in
   115	/-- **A mixed-parameter chart family is admissible input to the DAT-glue seam.**
   116	
   117	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` accepts it verbatim.  This is the statement that settles the
   118	question `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack` and I-0660 both left implicit: the representability engine
   119	never sees a chart parameter, so the forced calibration `b = n` is a *per-chart* condition and
   120	carries no uniformity obligation.
   121	
   122	Note what remains hypothetical here and is not weakened by this: `hf` (i.e. `IsChartUniv`, still
   123	CERT-Σ-gated), local surjectivity (DAT-B B-6), and the *existence* of `rep i` at parameters other
   124	than `g` — which is the question this observation hands to the divisor-representability lane. -/
   125	def mixedParamRepresentableBy {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
   126	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
   127	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
   128	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   129	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
   130	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
   131	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
   132	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i))
   133	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
   134	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))] :
   135	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
   136	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
   137	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
   138	  pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) hf
   139

     8	Layer-2 vehicle question (inbox I-0140), the extension is the *bespoke affine-opens
     9	limit*: a section over a test object `T` is a compatible family of plus classes over the
    10	affine opens of `T.left`, valued in `PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U)` via the section-ring
